title: Staggered Shift Corridor Coverage Estimator (ad-hoc)
summary: Small, fast spreadsheet to estimate who covers which corridor windows during a staggered-shift trial and the expected impact on token throughput / endpoint risk. Built for cross-functional scoping and quick handoffs.

content:
Purpose:
- Quick estimator used by product-ops + SRE to map staggered-shift coverage windows to estimated FTE and likely token-throughput impact. Not a final ROTA; intended to inform short-run staffing and fallbacks.

How to use:
1) Pick week/day and add a line for each coverage window (8h windows recommended but can be 6/4h).
2) Fill Primary and Backup, role (SRE, Infra Ops, Product-ops, SE), and fraction of FTE expected during that window.
3) Use historical traffic slices (see linked telemetry query) to estimate token/sec delta for a conservative-stress case.
4) Mark Risk level: Low/Medium/High and add Immediate actions (pre-warm, scaling policy changes, manual checks).

Assumptions (quick):
- "Normal" baseline throughput measured 2026-09-30 to 2026-10-06.
- Small-GPU pool pre-warm reduces cold-start risk for dedicated endpoints by ~60% (observed in experiment ENG-4551).
- FTE fractions assume partial overlap with other duties; not headcount authorizations.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Can Product schedule be shifted to avoid 10/13 canary deployment? (action: Leila to confirm by 2026-10-13 11:00)
- Who owns step 3 of manual failover runbook? (action: Samir to claim and add to runbook draft)
- Telemetry query to extract 95/99 latency during burst windows still needs validation (ticket: ENG-4823).

Notes on quick heuristics used for token/sec delta:
- If regional burst > 100k tokens/min, planned fallback to smaller-variant model reduces token cost but increases per-request latency; treat as medium risk.
- If dedicated-pool utilization crosses 85% for > 3 consecutive 1m buckets, classify as High risk and trigger reserve-burst.

Recent decisions captured here:
- Pre-warm policy for small-gpu pool approved by infra leads on 2026-09-28; action owner: Maya.
- Temporary 10% reserved burst capacity allocated to EU region for trial week 2026-10-12 -> 2026-10-18.

Row-level notes (freeform scratch):
- 00:00-08:00 window: likely low staffing in EU; make sure runbook includes contactable phone numbers for out-of-hours lead.
- 06:00-14:00 window: overlaps with scheduled canary 10/13; consider swapping Leila/Aaron to reduce cognitive load.
- 12:00-20:00 window: SRE backup coverage is single point today; escalate hiring / contractor plan if repeated High risk events appear.

Quick commands / links to run telemetry (paste these into the console):
- Telemetry burst query: metrics.query('model.request_tokens', group_by=['region','endpoint'], time_range='PT1H', agg='sum') with tag filter burst>100000
- Canary schedule: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RELEASES/Oct-2026-Canaries

Contact for this sheet: Maya Chen (maya@redwood.ai) — drop in slack #ops-oncall or DM for urgent changes.
